incidente.resumo: On 13 June 2023 in US-EAST-1, the Lambda Frontend fleet, while scaling, crossed a capacity threshold never reached within a single cell, triggering a latent software defect that left allocated Execution Environments unused; Lambda invocations in the affected cell saw increased errors and latencies, also affecting STS, the Management Console, EKS, Connect, EventBridge and others. Engineers initiated a scale down of the Frontend fleet below the triggering level; synchronous invocations recovered by 1:45 PM PDT and all services by 3:37 PM PDT.

descricao.texto: Starting at 11:49 AM PDT, customers experienced increased error rates and latencies for Lambda function invocations in US-EAST-1; the text does not say how the problem was first noticed.
trechos: Starting at 11:49 AM PDT on June 13th, 2023, customers experienced increased error rates and latencies for Lambda function invocations within the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region.

gatilho.texto: At 11:49 AM PDT, the Lambda Frontend fleet, scaling since 10:01 AM PDT in response to normal daily traffic growth, crossed a capacity threshold that had never been reached within a single cell.
trechos: At 10:01 AM PDT, the Lambda Frontend fleet started scaling in response to an increase in service traffic, within the normal daily traffic patterns, in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region.

At 11:49 AM PDT, the Lambda Frontend fleet, while adding additional compute capacity to handle the increase in service traffic, crossed a capacity threshold that had previously never been reached within a single cell.

descricao.texto: Crossing the threshold triggered a latent software defect that caused Lambda Execution Environments to be successfully allocated for incoming requests but never fully utilized by the Lambda Frontend; since Lambda could not provision new Execution Environments, invocations in the affected cell saw increased error rates and latencies.
trechos: This triggered a latent software defect which caused Lambda Execution Environments to be successfully allocated for incoming requests, but never fully utilized by the Lambda Frontend.
Since Lambda was not able to provision new Lambda Execution Environments for incoming requests, function invocations within the affected cell experienced increased error rates and latencies.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The authors state the event uncovered a gap in the Lambda cellular architecture for the scaling of the Lambda Frontend, which allowed a latent bug to cause impact as the affected cell scaled.
trechos: This event also uncovered a gap in our Lambda cellular architecture for the scaling of the Lambda Frontend, which allowed a latent bug to cause impact as the affected cell scaled.

passos.texto: After identifying the latent defect by 12:26 PM PDT, engineers confirmed traffic levels had subsided and initiated a scale down of the Lambda Frontend fleet to a level that no longer triggered the defect; by 1:30 PM PDT new invocations began to see recovery and by 1:45 PM PDT Lambda was fully recovered for synchronous invocations.
trechos: By 12:26 PM PDT, engineers had identified the latent software defect and the impact on the provisioning of underlying compute capacity.

As an immediate mitigation, engineers were able to confirm that traffic levels had subsided, and initiated a scale down of the Lambda Frontend fleet to a level that no longer triggered the latent software defect.
By 1:30 PM PDT, new Lambda function invocations began to see recovery.
By 1:45 PM PDT, Lambda was fully recovered for synchronous function invocations.

acoes.texto: Already done: the scaling activities for the Lambda Frontend fleet that triggered the event were immediately disabled while the latent bug was addressed.
trechos: We immediately disabled the scaling activities for the Lambda Frontend fleet activities that triggered the event, while we worked to address the latent bug that caused the issue; this bug has since been resolved and deployed to all Regions.

acoes.texto: Already done: the latent bug has been resolved and the fix deployed to all Regions.
trechos: We immediately disabled the scaling activities for the Lambda Frontend fleet activities that triggered the event, while we worked to address the latent bug that caused the issue; this bug has since been resolved and deployed to all Regions.

acoes.texto: Already done: Lambda completed several action items to address the immediate concern with cellular scaling.
trechos: Lambda has already completed several action items to address the immediate concern with cellular scaling and remains on track to complete a larger effort later this year to ensure that all cells are bounded to a well-tested size to avoid future unexpected scaling issues.

Starting at 11:49 AM PDT on June 13th, 2023, customers experienced increased error rates and latencies for Lambda function invocations within the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region.
Lambda function invocations began to return to normal levels at 1:45 PM PDT, and all affected services had fully recovered by 3:37 PM PDT.

observacoes: Duration computed from 11:49 AM PDT (start) to 1:45 PM PDT, when Lambda invocations returned to normal levels and synchronous invocations were fully recovered. Dependent services have their own windows (e.g. Management Console 11:48 AM to 2:02 PM, STS until 2:10 PM, Support Center until 2:38 PM PDT).
